findings.summary: The fault boundary calls write_fault_terminal(exception=exc) without a rounds count, so every fault terminal records rounds: 0 even when the line completed several rounds before crashing. fleet-sentinel and any operator reading terminal.json will see a crash after 7 rounds as rounds=0; rounds.jsonl still holds the true history, and the spec did not require the count, so this is observability polish rather than a defect in the required behaviour.

Spec section 1 and the Required tests describe the timeout streak as ending in a 'bounds' terminal, but streak_exceeded feeds check_bounds which returns TERMINAL_BLOCKED. That mapping is pre-existing and the spec's 'still ends in' wording asks for no change, so leaving it is correct; the required behaviour (typed timeout caught, worker_turn_timeout round appended, no crash, streak ends the line) is delivered and tested. Recorded independently, and it coincides with the Continuous reviewer's note.

The log path has two independent defaults: RunArtifacts derives LOG_ROOT/{folder_id}.log and LaunchSpec.log_file derives /data/fleet-graph/logs/{folder_id}.log, with no --log-path CLI flag to carry a non-default launcher log_path down to the line. They agree today because the scheduler never sets LaunchSpec.log_path, so a run root launched with an overridden log_path would advertise a log_path that does not name the file systemd is appending to.
